claim: Circadian disruption by light-at-night induced Purkinje cell death through pineal allopregnanolone (ALLO) activity during early life in chicks.
source: We showed that circadian disruption by light-at-night induced Purkinje cell death through pineal allopregnanolone (ALLO) activity during early life in chicks.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript including measurements of ALLO synthesis, Purkinje cell counts, and caspase-3 expression.

claim: Light-at-night caused the loss of diurnal variation of pineal ALLO synthesis during early life.
source: Light-at-night caused the loss of diurnal variation of pineal ALLO synthesis during early life and led to cerebellar Purkinje cell death, which was suppressed by a daily injection of ALLO.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 1 showing srd5a mRNA expression, ALLO synthesis, and ALLO concentration measurements under different light conditions.

claim: Daily injection of ALLO suppressed Purkinje cell death caused by light-at-night.
source: Light-at-night caused the loss of diurnal variation of pineal ALLO synthesis during early life and led to cerebellar Purkinje cell death, which was suppressed by a daily injection of ALLO.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 3 showing that ALLO injection decreased active caspase-3 expression and improved Purkinje cell survival.

claim: The loss of diurnal variation of pineal ALLO synthesis induced reduction in pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP), a neuroprotective hormone.
source: The loss of diurnal variation of pineal ALLO synthesis induced not only reduction in pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP), a neuroprotective hormone, but also transcriptional repression of the cerebellar Adcyap1 gene that produces PACAP, with subsequent Purkinje cell death.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5 showing PACAP mRNA expression changes under different light conditions and after pinealectomy.

claim: The loss of diurnal variation of pineal ALLO synthesis induced transcriptional repression of the cerebellar Adcyap1 gene that produces PACAP.
source: The loss of diurnal variation of pineal ALLO synthesis induced not only reduction in pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP), a neuroprotective hormone, but also transcriptional repression of the cerebellar Adcyap1 gene that produces PACAP, with subsequent Purkinje cell death.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 10 showing increased H3K9me3 levels at the Adcyap1 gene promoter under light-at-night conditions.

claim: Pineal ALLO mediated the effect of light on early cerebellar development in chicks.
source: Taken together, pineal ALLO mediated the effect of light on early cerebellar development in chicks.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the collective experimental data showing the pathway from light conditions to ALLO synthesis to PACAP expression to Purkinje cell survival.

claim: Circadian disruption by light-at-night affects weight gain in vertebrates during early neonatal or posthatch life.
source: Several studies have reported that circadian disruption by light-at-night affects weight gain in vertebrates during early neonatal or posthatch life (Brandon et al., 2002; Mann et al., 1986; Rozenboim et al., 2013; Takahashi et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: A light–dark cycle promotes better brain development than does constant light or constant darkness.
source: In addition, previous studies have demonstrated that a light–dark cycle promotes better brain development than does constant light or constant darkness (Bakkum et al., 1991; Brooks et al., 2011; Dulcis and Spitzer, 2008; Li et al., 2012; Ohta et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Little is known about the molecular mechanisms that control how environmental light conditions affect brain development.
source: However, little is known about the molecular mechanisms that control how environmental light conditions affect brain development.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field, representing a gap in understanding.

claim: The neuroendocrine system has a critical role in brain development in vertebrates.
source: The neuroendocrine system has a critical role in brain development in vertebrates, and its disruption induces abnormal development (Gore, 2008; León-Olea et al., 2014; Walker and Gore, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Disruption of the neuroendocrine system induces abnormal brain development.
source: The neuroendocrine system has a critical role in brain development in vertebrates, and its disruption induces abnormal development (Gore, 2008; León-Olea et al., 2014; Walker and Gore, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Neuroestrogen promotes Purkinje dendritic growth, spinogenesis, and synaptogenesis during neonatal life.
source: In the cerebellum, neuroestrogen promotes Purkinje dendritic growth, spinogenesis, and synaptogenesis during neonatal life (Haraguchi et al., 2012a; Sakamoto et al., 2003; Sasahara et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PACAP protects cerebellar granule cells from apoptosis through the inhibition of caspase-3 activity during development.
source: The pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) protects cerebellar granule cells from apoptosis through the inhibition of caspase-3 activity during development (Falluel-Morel et al., 2005; Vaudry et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Thyroid hormones regulate differentiation of neural cells, synaptogenesis, and myelination.
source: Thyroid hormones regulate differentiation of neural cells, synaptogenesis, and myelination (Bernal, 2007; Koibuchi and Chin, 2000; Pasquini et al., 1967).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: For normal cerebellar development, the developmental stage-specific action of various hormones is essential.
source: Therefore, for normal cerebellar development, the developmental stage-specific action of various hormones is essential.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies about hormone effects on cerebellar development.

claim: Multiple studies have suggested a link between light-at-night-induced circadian disruption and disruption of the neuroendocrine system.
source: Multiple studies have suggested a link between light-at-night-induced circadian disruption and disruption of the neuroendocrine system (Fonken and Nelson, 2014; Fonken et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Disruption of the neuroendocrine system is caused by exposure to light-at-night in the brain.
source: In the brain, disruption of the neuroendocrine system is caused by exposure to light-at-night (Fonken et al., 2009; Navara and Nelson, 2007; Reppert and Weaver, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Exposure to inappropriate lighting during early life disrupts hormone synthesis and causes abnormal development of the brain during early life.
source: Thus, previous studies have suggested that exposure to inappropriate lighting during early life disrupts hormone synthesis and causes abnormal development of the brain during early life.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies about light exposure and neuroendocrine disruption.

claim: The molecular mechanisms that modulate the expression of hormones depending on light conditions during early life are still incompletely understood.
source: However, the molecular mechanisms that modulate the expression of hormones depending on light conditions during early life are still incompletely understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field, representing a gap in understanding.

claim: The pineal gland actively produces a variety of steroids in birds.
source: Recently, we have demonstrated that the pineal gland, a photosensitive organ, actively produces a variety of steroids in birds (Haraguchi et al., 2012a; Hatori et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: Pineal allopregnanolone (ALLO) prevents the death of cerebellar Purkinje cells by suppressing apoptosis in chicks during development.
source: Importantly, pineal allopregnanolone (ALLO), a major pineal steroid, has been shown to prevent the death of cerebellar Purkinje cells by suppressing apoptosis in chicks during development (Haraguchi et al., 2012a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: The mRNA expression of 5α-reductase (srd5a) showed a marked diurnal change and was high during dark times (ZT16) in the pineal glands of LD chicks.
source: The mRNA expression of 5α-reductase (srd5a), a steroidogenic enzyme catalyzing the formation of ALLO, showed a marked diurnal change and was high during dark times (ZT16) in the pineal glands of LD chicks (Figure 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a measuring srd5a mRNA expression at different zeitgeber times.

claim: LL chicks showed consistently low srd5a mRNA levels in the pineal glands.
source: In contrast to the LD chicks, the LL chicks showed consistently low srd5a mRNA levels in the pineal glands (Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b measuring srd5a mRNA expression under constant light conditions.

claim: The elevation of srd5a mRNA during ZT16 in LD chicks was suppressed by light during ZT16, 1 hr after the light was put out in light-at-night chicks.
source: The elevation of srd5a mRNA during ZT16 in LD chicks was suppressed by light during ZT16, 1 hr after the light was put out in light-at-night chicks (Figure 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c measuring srd5a mRNA expression under light-at-night conditions.

claim: The ALLO concentration and synthesis were higher during ZT16 in the pineal glands of LD chicks than during ZT16 in the pineal glands of LL and light-at-night chicks.
source: In addition, the ALLO concentration and synthesis were higher during ZT16 in the pineal glands of LD chicks than during ZT16 in the pineal glands of LL and light-at-night chicks (Figure 1d,e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1d and 1e measuring ALLO synthesis and concentration.

claim: Cerebellar anterior lobe is the region that is the most vulnerable to the reduction of ALLO in the cerebellum.
source: Cerebellar anterior lobe is the region that is the most vulnerable to the reduction of ALLO in the cerebellum (Haraguchi et al., 2012a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: LL conditions increased the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobule IV (p=0.0027) and lobule V (p=0.0304) of cerebellar vermis on posthatch day 7 (P7) male chicks compared with LD conditions.
source: Compared with LD conditions, LL (lobule IV, p=0.0027; lobule V, p=0.0304) and light-at-night (lobule III, p=0.0129; lobule IV, p=0.0011; lobule V, p=0.0136) conditions increased the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobules III-V of cerebellar vermis on posthatch day 7 (P7) male chicks (Figure 2c,d and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c,d and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 with statistical analysis.

claim: Light-at-night conditions increased the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobule III (p=0.0129), lobule IV (p=0.0011), and lobule V (p=0.0136) of cerebellar vermis on posthatch day 7 (P7) male chicks compared with LD conditions.
source: Compared with LD conditions, LL (lobule IV, p=0.0027; lobule V, p=0.0304) and light-at-night (lobule III, p=0.0129; lobule IV, p=0.0011; lobule V, p=0.0136) conditions increased the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobules III-V of cerebellar vermis on posthatch day 7 (P7) male chicks (Figure 2c,d and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c,d and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 with statistical analysis.

claim: Active caspase-3 positive cells were increased in lobule IV of female chicks by light-at-night.
source: Active caspase-3 positive cells were also increased in lobule IV of female chicks by light-at-night (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a.

claim: LL conditions decreased the number of Purkinje cells in lobule III (p=0.0001) and lobule IV (p=0.0005) of cerebellar vermis at P21 chicks compared with LD conditions.
source: Compared with LD conditions, LL (lobule III, p=0.0001; lobule IV, p=0.0005) and light-at-night (lobule III, p<0.0001; lobule IV, p<0.0001; lobule V, p=0.0205) conditions decreased the number of Purkinje cells in lobules III-V of cerebellar vermis at P21 chicks (Figure 2e,f and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e,f and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 with statistical analysis.

claim: Light-at-night conditions decreased the number of Purkinje cells in lobule III (p<0.0001), lobule IV (p<0.0001), and lobule V (p=0.0205) of cerebellar vermis at P21 chicks compared with LD conditions.
source: Compared with LD conditions, LL (lobule III, p=0.0001; lobule IV, p=0.0005) and light-at-night (lobule III, p<0.0001; lobule IV, p<0.0001; lobule V, p=0.0205) conditions decreased the number of Purkinje cells in lobules III-V of cerebellar vermis at P21 chicks (Figure 2e,f and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e,f and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 with statistical analysis.

claim: Purkinje cell numbers were decreased in lobule IV of female chicks by light-at-night.
source: Purkinje cell numbers were also decreased in lobule IV of female chicks by light-at-night (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1b.

claim: There was no significant difference in the thickness of the molecular layer of Purkinje cells in lobule IV among LD, LL, or light-at-night chicks.
source: In contrast to the number of Purkinje cells, there was no significant difference in the thickness of the molecular layer of Purkinje cells in lobule IV among LD, LL, or light-at-night chicks (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Purkinje cell numbers were decreased in lobules III-V of cerebellar vermis by light-at-night during the P1–P7 period in adulthood.
source: In adulthood, Purkinje cell numbers were also decreased in lobules III-V of cerebellar vermis by light-at-night during the P1–P7 period (Figure 2g and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2g and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Light-at-night conditions induce disruption of diurnal variation in pineal ALLO and lead to Purkinje cell death in the cerebellum.
source: These results suggest that light-at-night conditions induce disruption of diurnal variation in pineal ALLO and lead to Purkinje cell death in the cerebellum.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing the relationship between light conditions, ALLO synthesis, and Purkinje cell death.

claim: Daily injection of ALLO in light-at-night chicks from P1 to P7 decreased active caspase-3 expression in lobule IV at P7.
source: Compared with light-at-night chicks, daily injection of ALLO in light-at-night chicks from P1 to P7 decreased active caspase-3 expression in lobule IV at P7 and improved Purkinje cell survival in lobule IV at P21 (Figure 3b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Daily injection of ALLO in light-at-night chicks from P1 to P7 improved Purkinje cell survival in lobule IV at P21.
source: Compared with light-at-night chicks, daily injection of ALLO in light-at-night chicks from P1 to P7 decreased active caspase-3 expression in lobule IV at P7 and improved Purkinje cell survival in lobule IV at P21 (Figure 3b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Pineal ALLO suppresses the apoptosis of Purkinje cells during early life.
source: These results suggest that pineal ALLO suppresses the apoptosis of Purkinje cells during early life.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing that ALLO injection reduces caspase-3 expression and improves Purkinje cell survival.

claim: ALLO acts as an agonist of the γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptor.
source: ALLO acts as an agonist of the γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptor and may act as an agonist of the membrane progesterone receptors α (mPRα), mPRβ, and mPRγ, and the pregnane X receptor (PXR) (Belelli and Lambert, 2005; Frye et al., 2011; Langmade et al., 2006; Pang et al., 2013; Schumacher et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: ALLO may act as an agonist of the membrane progesterone receptors α (mPRα), mPRβ, and mPRγ, and the pregnane X receptor (PXR).
source: ALLO acts as an agonist of the γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptor and may act as an agonist of the membrane progesterone receptors α (mPRα), mPRβ, and mPRγ, and the pregnane X receptor (PXR) (Belelli and Lambert, 2005; Frye et al., 2011; Langmade et al., 2006; Pang et al., 2013; Schumacher et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and uses speculative language ('may act').

claim: RT-PCR analyses demonstrated the expression of the α1-subunit of the GABAA receptor, mPRα, mPRβ, and mPRγ in chick cerebella.
source: The RT-PCR analyses demonstrated the expression of the α1-subunit of the GABAA receptor, mPRα, mPRβ, and mPRγ but did not detect the expression of PXR in chick cerebella (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: RT-PCR analyses did not detect the expression of PXR in chick cerebella.
source: The RT-PCR analyses demonstrated the expression of the α1-subunit of the GABAA receptor, mPRα, mPRβ, and mPRγ but did not detect the expression of PXR in chick cerebella (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Silencing of mPRα increased the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobule IV of P7 chicks relative to the number in the control siRNA.
source: Silencing of mPRα increased the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobule IV of P7 chicks relative to the number in the control siRNA (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: A daily injection of ALLO did not prevent the activation of caspase-3 in Purkinje cells in mPRα siRNA-transfected chicks.
source: A daily injection of ALLO did not prevent the activation of caspase-3 in Purkinje cells in mPRα siRNA-transfected chicks (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Transfection of siRNAs for mPRβ and mPRγ into the cerebellum of newly hatched male chicks did not change the expression of active caspase-3 in Purkinje cells from that of the control siRNA-transfected chicks.
source: By contrast, transfection of siRNAs for mPRβ and mPRγ into the cerebellum of newly hatched male chicks did not change the expression of active caspase-3 in Purkinje cells from that of the control siRNA-transfected chicks (Figure 4c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4c and 4d.

claim: A daily injection of isoALLO did not change the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobule IV of P7 chicks relative to the number in the control chicks.
source: A daily injection of isoALLO did not change the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobule IV of P7 chicks relative to the number in the control chicks (Figure 4e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: mPRα may function as a receptor for pineal ALLO in the developing cerebellum.
source: These results suggest that mPRα may function as a receptor for pineal ALLO in the developing cerebellum.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing that mPRα silencing increases caspase-3 expression and prevents ALLO's protective effects.

claim: Distinct mPRα immunoreactivity was observed in the Purkinje cells.
source: Distinct mPRα immunoreactivity was observed in the Purkinje cells (Figure 4f).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4f.

claim: Saturation analysis and Scatchard plots show the presence of a high-affinity (dissociation constant, 11.8 ± 3.1 nM), limited-capacity (maximal binding capacity, 0.91 ± 0.29 nM), saturable, single-binding site for [3H]-ALLO in the membrane fraction of the COS-7 cells transfected with chicken mPRα cDNA.
source: Saturation analysis and Scatchard plots show the presence of a high-affinity (dissociation constant, 11.8 ± 3.1 nM), limited-capacity (maximal binding capacity, 0.91 ± 0.29 nM), saturable, single-binding site for [3H]-ALLO in the membrane fraction of the COS-7 cells transfected with chicken mPRα cDNA (Figure 4g).
evidence: This claim is supported by radioreceptor assay data shown in Figure 4g.

claim: Fluorescein-labeled ALLO bound to COS-7 cells expressing mPRα.
source: Confocal fluorescence microscopy revealed that fluorescein-labeled ALLO bound to COS-7 cells expressing mPRα and that an excess of ALLO competed with fluorescein-labeled ALLO for binding to COS-7 cells expressing mPRα (Figure 4i and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4i and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: An excess of ALLO competed with fluorescein-labeled ALLO for binding to COS-7 cells expressing mPRα.
source: Confocal fluorescence microscopy revealed that fluorescein-labeled ALLO bound to COS-7 cells expressing mPRα and that an excess of ALLO competed with fluorescein-labeled ALLO for binding to COS-7 cells expressing mPRα (Figure 4i and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4i and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pinealectomy (Px) at P1 decreased the expression of PACAP and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) mRNAs at P7.
source: Pinealectomy (Px) at P1 decreased the expression of PACAP and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) mRNAs at P7 (Figure 5a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Px did not influence the expression of neurotrophin-3 (NT-3), cytochrome P450 aromatase (P450arom), 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (3β-HSD), type II deiodinase (Dio2), and insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-1) mRNAs.
source: On the other hand, Px did not influence the expression of neurotrophin-3 (NT-3), cytochrome P450 aromatase (P450arom), 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (3β-HSD), type II deiodinase (Dio2), and insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-1) mRNAs (Figure 5a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: A daily injection of ALLO in Px chicks increased the expression of PACAP relative to that in Px chicks.
source: In addition, a daily injection of ALLO in Px chicks increased the expression of PACAP relative to that in Px chicks (Figure 5a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The expression of PACAP mRNA showed a marked diurnal change in the cerebellum and was high during dark times (ZT16 and ZT20) in LD chicks.
source: The expression of PACAP mRNA showed a marked diurnal change in the cerebellum and was high during dark times (ZT16 and ZT20) in LD chicks (Figure 5b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The elevation of PACAP mRNA at ZT16 in LD chicks was suppressed at ZT16 in light-at-night chicks.
source: The elevation of PACAP mRNA at ZT16 in LD chicks was suppressed at ZT16 in light-at-night chicks (Figure 5b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Px increased the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobule IV of P7 chicks relative to those in the control.
source: Px increased the number of Purkinje cells that expressed active caspase-3 in lobule IV of P7 chicks relative to those in the control (Figure 5c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: A daily injection of ALLO or PACAP in Px chicks decreased the number of Purkinje cells expressing active caspase-3 in lobule IV at P7.
source: A daily injection of ALLO or PACAP in Px chicks decreased the number of Purkinje cells expressing active caspase-3 in lobule IV at P7 (Figure 5c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Px at P1 decreased the number of Purkinje cells in lobule IV at P21.
source: Px at P1 decreased the number of Purkinje cells in lobule IV at P21 (Figure 5d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: A daily injection of ALLO or PACAP in Px chicks from P1 to P7 improved Purkinje cell survival in lobule IV at P21.
source: A daily injection of ALLO or PACAP in Px chicks from P1 to P7 improved Purkinje cell survival in lobule IV at P21 (Figure 5d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Clear PACAP and PAC1 immunoreactivities were observed in Purkinje cells.
source: Clear PACAP and PAC1 immunoreactivities were observed in Purkinje cells (Figure 5e,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 5e and 5f.

claim: PACAP mediates the neuroprotective action of pineal ALLO during early life.
source: These results suggest that PACAP mediates the neuroprotective action of pineal ALLO during early life.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing that ALLO induces PACAP expression and both have similar neuroprotective effects.

claim: Light-at-night chicks showed a decreased Purkinje cell number at P21 relative to that in the control.
source: Light-at-night chicks showed a decreased Purkinje cell number at P21 relative to that in the control, but daily injections of ALLO in light-at-night chicks from P8 to P14 did not rescue Purkinje cells from death in lobule IV at P21 and, furthermore, did not suppress the expression of active caspase-3 in lobule IV at P14 (Figure 6b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6b and 6c.

claim: Daily injections of ALLO in light-at-night chicks from P8 to P14 did not rescue Purkinje cells from death in lobule IV at P21.
source: Light-at-night chicks showed a decreased Purkinje cell number at P21 relative to that in the control, but daily injections of ALLO in light-at-night chicks from P8 to P14 did not rescue Purkinje cells from death in lobule IV at P21 and, furthermore, did not suppress the expression of active caspase-3 in lobule IV at P14 (Figure 6b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6b and 6c.

claim: Daily injections of ALLO in light-at-night chicks from P8 to P14 did not suppress the expression of active caspase-3 in lobule IV at P14.
source: Light-at-night chicks showed a decreased Purkinje cell number at P21 relative to that in the control, but daily injections of ALLO in light-at-night chicks from P8 to P14 did not rescue Purkinje cells from death in lobule IV at P21 and, furthermore, did not suppress the expression of active caspase-3 in lobule IV at P14 (Figure 6b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6b and 6c.

claim: The neuroprotective actions of pineal ALLO on Purkinje cells are restricted during the first week posthatch.
source: In summary, the neuroprotective actions of pineal ALLO on Purkinje cells are restricted during the first week posthatch.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing that ALLO is effective during P1-P7 but not during P8-P14.

claim: Daily injection of PACAP in light-at-night chicks from P1 to P7 decreased active caspase-3 expression in lobule IV at P7 relative to that in light-at-night chicks.
source: Daily injection of PACAP in light-at-night chicks from P1 to P7 decreased active caspase-3 expression in lobule IV at P7 relative to that in light-at-night chicks and improved Purkinje cell survival in lobule IV at P21 (Figure 7b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Daily injection of PACAP in light-at-night chicks from P1 to P7 improved Purkinje cell survival in lobule IV at P21.
source: Daily injection of PACAP in light-at-night chicks from P1 to P7 decreased active caspase-3 expression in lobule IV at P7 relative to that in light-at-night chicks and improved Purkinje cell survival in lobule IV at P21 (Figure 7b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: Daily injection of PACAP in light-at-night chicks from P8 to P14 suppressed the expression of active caspase-3 expression in lobule IV at P14.
source: Compared with the control, light-at-night chicks were found to have a decreased Purkinje cell number at P21, and daily injection of PACAP in light-at-night chicks from P8 to P14 suppressed the expression of active caspase-3 expression in lobule IV at P14 and rescued Purkinje cells in lobule IV at P21 (Figure 7e,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7e.

claim: Daily injection of PACAP in light-at-night chicks from P8 to P14 rescued Purkinje cells in lobule IV at P21.
source: Compared with the control, light-at-night chicks were found to have a decreased Purkinje cell number at P21, and daily injection of PACAP in light-at-night chicks from P8 to P14 suppressed the expression of active caspase-3 expression in lobule IV at P14 and rescued Purkinje cells in lobule IV at P21 (Figure 7e,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7f.

claim: The neuroprotective actions of PACAP on Purkinje cells were not restricted during the first week posthatch.
source: In summary, the neuroprotective actions of PACAP on Purkinje cells were not restricted during the first week posthatch.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing that PACAP is effective during both P1-P7 and P8-P14 periods.

claim: Px at P8 decreased PACAP expression in the cerebellum at P14 relative to that in the control.
source: Px at P8 decreased PACAP expression in the cerebellum at P14 relative to that in the control (Figure 8a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8a.

claim: A daily injection of ALLO in Px at P8 chicks from P8 to P14 did not induce the expression of PACAP mRNA.
source: A daily injection of ALLO in Px at P8 chicks from P8 to P14 did not induce the expression of PACAP mRNA (Figure 8a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8a.

claim: PACAP expression decreased gradually according to the maturation of the cerebellum during early life.
source: In addition, we demonstrated that PACAP expression decreased gradually according to the maturation of the cerebellum during early life (Figure 8b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8b.

claim: Trimethylation of lysine 9 or 27 on histone H3 and lysine 20 on histone H4 (H3K9me3, H3K27me3, and H4K20me3) is associated with transcriptional repression.
source: Trimethylation of lysine 9 or 27 on histone H3 and lysine 20 on histone H4 (H3K9me3, H3K27me3, and H4K20me3) is associated with transcriptional repression.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about histone modifications.
